Package architecture

Source: vignettes/articles/architecture.Rmd
architecture.Rmd

This page is for people who want to read, modify, or extend spDBL. It maps the workflow functions to the code that implements them. For the statistical model, see vignette("calibration-details") and Banerjee et al. (2025).

Layers

Layer Files What lives there
Workflow API R/func_wrapper.R, R/calibration_prepare.R, R/calibration_fit.R prepare_data(), emulator_learn(), emulator_predict(), calibration_prepare(), calibration_validate(), calibration_fit(), calibration_predict(), and the S3 methods for spDBL_calibration
Dynamic linear model kernels R/func_FF.R, R/func_BS.R, R/func_FFBS.R Forward filter, backward sampler, posterior sampling and prediction for each covariance model
Out of core R/func_FF.R (FF_bigdata_R()), R/func_bigdata.R Filter, smoother and exact predictor that stream CSV blocks from disk
Compiled kernels src/FF.cpp, src/BS.cpp, src/rmn.cpp (RcppEigen) One forward-filter step, one backward-smoothing step, matrix-normal draws
Calibration internals R/calibration_recover.R, inst/stan/*.stan Stan data assembly, the two Stan programs, R reference log densities, recovery of discrepancy and field draws
Distributions R/func_MNIW.R, R/func_MNIW_sampler.R, R/func_lppd_ana.R MNIW/MNIG updates and samplers, matrix-T density, one-step log predictive densities
Data and design construction R/func_gen_data.R, R/func_generate_grid_Dan.R Kernels, autoregressive design matrices, episode partitioning, grid traversal, synthetic data
Simulator and legacy helpers R/func_calibrate.R The SIR reaction–diffusion simulator (SIR(), gen_pde()) and helpers from the original research code
Plotting R/func_plot.R Heatmap panels and interval summaries

Covariance models and naming

The emulator is a matrix-variate dynamic linear model. Its right (spatial) covariance has three forms, and kernel functions carry a matching suffix:

Model Suffix Example functions Available in emulator_learn()
Inverse-Wishart Σ none FF(), FFBS(), FFBS_sampling() covariance = "iw" (default)
σ² R, R fixed _sigma2R FF_sigma2R(), FFBS_sigma2R(), FFBS_sampling_sigma2R() covariance = "sigma2R" (required for calibration)
Identity _I FF_I(), FFBS_I(), FFBS_sampling_I() no; kernel functions only

Emulation: what emulator_learn() does

  1. Validates the grid (Nx, Ny), the blocking (episode_window must divide Nx), and the kernel settings.
  2. Builds two exponential kernels with range 3 / (gp_tune * max distance): V over simulator inputs and R_episode over the sites of one spatial block. The full-grid R_field (S × S) is not formed unless supplied; only calibration uses it, and .cal_R_field() builds it at the observed sites.
  3. Splits each time step’s field into B = Nx / episode_window spatial blocks (generate.grid.rowsnake()). Every (time, block) pair is one episode of the dynamic model; this is the dynamic transfer-learning partition.
  4. Builds the autoregressive design for every episode with gen_F_ls_AR1_EP() or gen_F_ls_AR2_EP(), unless F_ls_train is given.
  5. Runs forward filtering and backward smoothing: FFBS() or FFBS_sigma2R(). The inverse-Wishart forward step is in C++ (FF_1step_cpp); the σ² R step is in R (FF_1step_R_sigma2R()); every backward step calls BS_1step_cpp.
  6. Draws nsam posterior samples with FFBS_sampling() or FFBS_sampling_sigma2R(). sampling = "marginal" draws each episode’s smoothed marginal given a shared covariance draw; sampling = "joint" draws whole coefficient paths.
  7. Returns an object of class spDBL_emulator with para_ffbs (filtering and smoothing moments), res_ffbs (posterior draws), and setup (every setting and design needed for prediction).

emulator_predict() calls FFBS_predict_exact() (default) or FFBS_predict_MC() (MC = TRUE), then maps episodes back to the time × space layout with recover_from_EP_exact() or recover_from_EP_MC(). Given the output of calibration_prepare(), it predicts with GP-interpolated design rows instead, so no new simulator runs are needed.

Calibration: from emulator to posterior

  1. calibration_prepare() requires a "sigma2R" emulator. It reuses the emulator’s draws or resamples them (sample_calibration_emulator()), then make_offline_calibration_input() fits the design-row GP (fit_offline_ar2(); by default a Matern 5/2 kernel with one length scale per input and separate hyperparameters for each time step) and caches Cholesky factors. Result: class spDBL_calibration_input. predict_calibration() turns one coefficient draw into the field mean and covariance at an input. With design_uncertainty = TRUE (the default) the covariance includes the design GP’s error, as a rank-N factor per time (.cal_design_factors()).
  2. calibration_validate() compares these PDE-free predictions with held-out simulations.
  3. calibration_fit() validates the settings, compiles or loads the Stan program (.cal_stan_model()), and calls fit_calibration_rstan(). That function runs one conditional Stan fit per emulator draw and pools an equal number of samples from each fit. Result: class spDBL_calibration, with summary(), print() and plot() methods.
  4. calibration_predict() recovers discrepancy paths (recover_calibration_discrepancy()) and field draws (recover_calibration_predictions()).

There are two Stan programs in inst/stan/:

  • calibration_marginal.stan, the default (marginal_discrepancy = TRUE), integrates the discrepancy states out with a Kalman filter.
  • calibration_offline.stan samples the discrepancy innovations explicitly.

Both integrate out the emulator field analytically. R reference implementations of the same log densities (calibration_log_density(), calibration_marginal_log_density()) let the tests check the Stan code.

Large grids out of core

For grids too large to hold every episode in memory, three functions stream CSV blocks from disk (R/func_FF.R, R/func_bigdata.R):

  1. FF_bigdata_R() filters forward and writes each time step’s filtered moments, all blocks side by side, to one set of CSV files.
  2. BS_bigdata_R() reads those files backwards, one time step at a time, and writes the smoothed moments.
  3. FFBS_predict_bigdata_R() streams each block’s responses, designs and smoothed means, and writes one prediction file per time step.

Memory holds one time step of moments and one data block at a time. The tests check all three against the in-memory FF(), BS() and FFBS_predict_exact(). Prediction needs every training run in each block (bnrow = fnrow), as emulator_learn() arranges them.

Reproducibility mechanisms

  • Every function that takes a seed sets it locally and restores the caller’s random-number state on exit (.cal_seed()).
  • Compiled Stan models are cached in memory and on disk (tools::R_user_dir("spDBL", "cache"), or cache_dir). The cache key combines the Stan file’s MD5 hash and the R, rstan, StanHeaders and platform versions, so editing a Stan file triggers a recompile.
  • calibration_fit(checkpoint_dir = ...) saves each conditional fit to disk as it finishes. Nothing reloads these files automatically; a rerun starts again from the first emulator draw.
  • calibration_fit() records execution_only = TRUE when there is no warmup or fewer than two post-warmup iterations, as with iter = 1. iter has no default, so every analysis states its sampler settings.

Extending spDBL

  • A new covariance model needs a one-step forward filter, a sampler for the covariance, an FFBS_*()/FFBS_sampling_*() pair, and a new covariance option in emulator_learn(). The _sigma2R functions are the closest template.
  • A new input kernel: the exponential kernel and its range heuristic are defined inside emulator_learn(); FFBS_predict_exact() and the calibration code read the stored phi_para, gp_sigma2, and gp_tau2.
  • A new sampling backend: calibration_fit(backend = ) accepts only "rstan" today. The backend-specific code is .cal_stan_model() and fit_calibration_rstan().

Tests

The tests are in tests/testthat/. The calibration tests compare the Gaussian conditioning, the Stan log densities, and the pooled sampler with independent R calculations. Tests that compile Stan are skipped unless SPDBL_RUN_STAN_TESTS=true; the coverage workflow on GitHub Actions turns them on. See the contributing guide for how to run tests and coverage locally.

Known limitations

  • The out-of-core path covers filtering, smoothing and exact (mean) prediction. Posterior sampling and calibration work in memory.
  • The delta (discount) argument of the one-step filters is accepted but not used.
  • Calibration supports the σ² R emulator only, with a fixed discrepancy covariance scale U, complete observations, and the training grid and times.
  • The design-row error is treated as independent across observation times, although it is in fact persistent; see vignette("calibration-details").
